[MUQATIL:79:15-26/r6] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The call to purify oneself means repairing what one has corrupted and accepting the invitation to God's oneness.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Ambiguous, non-fully-declinable adverbs include أين، متى، كيف، حيث، إذ، إذا، قبل and بعد; they are not freely inflected or indefinite and resemble interjections or non-nouns.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalīl says من عل is treated more like a declinable form; when adjusted like قبل and بعد, it is vocalized like أول and the vocative حكم.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | أول and حكم retain more declinable behavior than forms such as الذي and من, so speakers resist reducing them to the invariant pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When one of these adverbs becomes a person's name, its form changes like لو، هل، بل، ليت and ذا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalīl treats أول in مذ عام أول as an adjective with من عامك omitted, while أول can also be a noun; عام أول means the prior year, and أول من أمس and بعد غد likewise use omitted comparisons.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ابدأ به أول omits من كذا; comparison can be stated, but frequent use makes omission common there and required in عام أول.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | A rare مذ عام أول treats أول as an adverb meaning before your year.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In زيد أسفل منك, أسفل is an adverb meaning Zayd is in a place below yours, parallel to والركب أسفل منكم. | mentions 8:42
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | لا عليك, هل لك في ذلك and من له في ذلك omit an understood حاجة; frequent usage makes the ellipsis clear.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | The poetic أولا can be either an adjective or an adverb.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | دون، فوق، تحت، قبل and بعد behave as declinable nouns because they take complements and occur outside adverbial use; some speakers analogize من فوق and من تحت to قبل and بعد.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When two unvowelled consonants meet in these forms, speakers vocalize the latter; if its predecessor is vowelled, it stays still, as in هل، بل، أجل، نعم and جير.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Poetry attests to من تحت، من عل and من أمامه، من دون.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | prefers | Al-Khalīl regards من أمام، من قدام and related forms as indefinite unless attached to a definite noun; Arab usage supports him, against Yūnus's analysis of من قدام as definite and feminine.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | rejects | Yūnus treats من قدام as definite and diptote because he considers it feminine, but Sībawayh says no Arab he consulted uses that analysis.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r23] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | The ʿAlawiyyīn and Tamīmī informants use من قديديمة and من وريئة as indefinite, like صباحا، مساء، عشية and ضحوة.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r24] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Accusatives such as أماما and خلفا follow the pattern of يمنة and شأمة; al-Jaʿdī gives a poetic example.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r25] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | جاء من أسفل uses أسفل as an أفعل comparison form, as in the Qur'anic phrase about arrival from above and below. | mentions 33:10
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Terminal forms such as قبل، بعد and حيث take ḍamma; some speakers analogize حيث to أين.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | قبل and بعد are non-fully-declinable because they cannot stand independently in a clause like ordinary nouns; their invariant use across times resembles particles.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | لدن is jussive and less versatile than عند, so is treated like قط; قط and حسب are non-fully-declinable for ‘only,’ and قط can denote a temporal limit.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | لد is shortened from لدن; before attached pronouns the full form returns, as in من لدنه and من لدني, and لدن resembles عن.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | reports | Al-Khalīl says مع is accusative because it is used as an independent noun in معا and as an adverb with pronouns, like أمام and قدام.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Al-Rāʿī's verse makes معكم rhyme like هل under poetic necessity.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالظروفالمبهمةغيرالمتمكنة)#549/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Since takes ḍamma partly by the tendency to follow one ḍamma with another, as in رد يا فتى.
[TAB-FULL:v24p81/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Moses invites Pharaoh to cleanse himself of disbelief and believe in his Lord.
[TAB-FULL:v24p81/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd says تزكى means submit to Islam, and interprets the same wording throughout the Qur’an as Islam, citing 20:76, 80:3, and 80:7. | mentions 20:76, 80:3, 80:7
[TAB-FULL:v24p81/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · عكرمة | reports | ʿIkrima takes Moses’ invitation as a call to profess that there is no god but God.
[TAB-FULL:v24p81/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Medinan readers generally pronounce the zāy doubled, while Kufan and Basran readers generally pronounce it light.
[TAB-FULL:v24p81/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · أبو عمرو | rejects | Abū ʿAmr’s intensified reading is explained as “give alms,” from تتزكى with assimilation; al-Ṭabarī rejects that sense because Moses called Pharaoh to Islam, not charity while he was an unbeliever.
[TAB-FULL:v24p81/r6] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | prefers | Al-Ṭabarī says the light pronunciation is more eloquent; in context تزكى means becoming a pure believer.
[NAHHAS:v5p143/r8] NAHHAS, d. 338 · أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو | reports | They read تزكى with a light zāy; its meaning and Arabic analysis are the same as the doubled reading because the original form is تتزكى.
[NAHHAS:v5p143/r9] NAHHAS, d. 338 · ابن زيد | reports | He explains تزكى as becoming Muslim and says every occurrence of تزكية in the Quran means Islam.
[IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p362#2/r2] IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA, d. 370 · author | holds | The light form means “be pure”; the doubled form means “give alms.” Moses would not ask Pharaoh, knowing his unbelief, to give charity; “zakiyya,” not “mutazakkiya,” supports this. | mentions 18:74
[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p374/r1] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · ابن كثير ونافع | reports | Ibn Kathīr and Nāfiʿ read تزكى with a doubled zāy.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p374/r2] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · عاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي | reports | ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read تزكى with a light zāy.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p374/r3] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · عباس عن أبي عمرو | reports | ʿAbbās transmits a doubled zāy reading from Abū ʿAmr, like Nāfiʿ’s.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p374/r4] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · author | holds | Al-Fārisī explains the invitation as a call to purify oneself from shirk, citing the purification wording in 91:9, 18:74, and 80:7. | mentions 91:9, 18:74, 80:7
[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p374/r5] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · author | holds | The clause omits its subject in wording but implies هل لك إلى ذلك حاجة أو إربة (whether you have a need or desire for that).
[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p374/r6] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · الشاعر | reports | The poet’s هل لكم فيها إلي construction is cited as evidence for this use of إلى with هل لك.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p374/r7] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · author | holds | The doubled-zāy reading derives from تتزكى, with the tāʾ assimilated into zāy because of their proximity.
[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p374/r8] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · author | holds | The light-zāy reading drops the tāʾ represented in the assimilated form; al-Fārisī says deletion and lightening is the more natural analysis.
[SULAMI:v2p370#3/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · ابن عطاء | reports | The invitation is to be cleansed of the sins that stain one and returned to servanthood, the station of honor and salvation.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r10] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · قتادة | reports | Tazakka here means to become Muslim.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v6p197/r11] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · الكلبي | reports | Tazakka can mean to do good.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r3] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | reports | An interpretation promises that saying 'There is no god but God' brings an imperishable kingdom, unaging youth, four hundred years of joy and comfort, and then paradise.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r5] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | reports | Although Moses spoke with utmost gentleness, God's hidden decree turned Pharaoh's heart away, planted refusal, and prevented him from accepting counsel.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p186/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | To purify oneself means to become free of associating partners with God, as in 91:9 and the description in 18:74. | mentions 91:9, 18:74
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p186/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The wording omits a required noun; the sense is, “Do you have a need or desire for that?”
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p186/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | reports | An unattributed line about having a need for someone illustrates the elliptical construction and implied desire.

[JISHUMI:v10p7268/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير ويعقوب | reports | These readers double the zāy in يزكى, construing it as an elided form of تتزكى.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r18] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Purification means cleansing oneself of deficiencies and taking on virtues; reducing it to conversion or the declaration of God’s oneness is too narrow, since the broader sense includes both.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r19] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · ابن كثير، نافع، أبو عمرو | reports | They read tazakkā with a doubled zāy; the reading is also reported from Abu ʿAmr with variation.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r20] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الباقون | reports | The remaining readers read tazakkā with a light zāy.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#3/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن كثير ونافع | reports | Ibn Kathīr and Nāfiʿ read tazakkā with a doubled zāy, meaning to purify oneself from polytheism.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p37/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The idiom “hal laka ilā” resembles “hal laka fī” (“do you desire it?”); another possible ellipsis is “is there a way to become purified?”
[RAZI-FULL:v31p37/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الواحدي | reports | Al-Wāḥidī supplies an implicit subject: “Do you have a need or purpose to become purified?”
[RAZI-FULL:v31p37/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | An anonymous poetic line beginning “fa-hal lakum fīhā ilayya” witnesses this idiom; al-Rāzī also allows an implied “way” to purification.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p37/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Zakī means pure from every defect, as in the account of the slain youth and the successful soul that is purified. | mentions 18:74, 91:9
[RAZI-FULL:v31p37/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The invitation gathers all Moses’ call: become purified from what is unfitting through embracing both monotheism and religious law.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p37/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | The word has a doubled reading by assimilating the tāʾ of the reflexive form into the nearby zāy, and a light reading.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p37/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المعتزلة | reports | The Muʿtazilites argue that the question treats purification as a path Moses’ addressee can choose; if God caused it, Moses’ appeal would be turned against him.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p37/r8] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | rejects | Al-Rāzī says the answer to this kind of argument has already been given.
[RAZI-FULL:v31p37/r9] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Moses’ invitation follows the command to speak gently to Pharaoh; the Qur’an’s instruction to Muhammad likewise shows that calling to God requires kindness, restraint, and avoiding harshness. | mentions 20:44, 3:159
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r12] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The invitation is to become Muslim and be purified of sins.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن عباس | reports | Al-Dahhak transmits Ibn Abbas’s interpretation as a call to testify that there is no god but God.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r15] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · نافع | reports | Nafiʿ and Ibn Kathir double zāy by assimilating the original tāʾ of tatazakkā.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r16] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | The other readers use a light zāy, with the tāʾ dropped.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r17] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو عمرو | prefers | Abu ʿAmr says the doubled form means give charity and the light form become a pure believer; he selects the latter as Moses invited Pharaoh to belief.
[QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r18] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · صخر بن جويرية | reports | Sakhr ibn Juwayriyya reports Moses asking how to approach Pharaoh when he knew he would refuse; God ordered him to go and said twelve thousand angels seek knowledge of the decree without attaining it.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Moses asks whether Pharaoh is inclined to purify himself from disbelief and rebellion.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · الحجازيان ويعقوب | reports | The Hijazis and Yaqub read the verb with shadda.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#9/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The invitation asks whether Pharaoh is inclined to purify himself from idolatry and disobedience through obedience and faith.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#9/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · حجازى | reports | A Hijazi reading geminates the zāy in تزكى.
[QASHANI:79:18-26/r1] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Purification means annihilating selfhood; guidance to fear is knowledge of the unity of the Essence, which softens and dissolves selfhood.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p397/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | هل لك إلى أن تزكى is a gentle invitation that any reasonable person would accept.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Purification means acquiring virtues and cleansing vices; here it includes Islam and God’s oneness.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الحرميان وأبو عمرو | reports | The two Medinan readers and Abū ʿAmr, with the stated qualification, double the zāy and ṣād; the rest of the Seven lighten them.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | هل لك إلى omits the object of إلى, understood as desire, need, or way toward something; an unnamed poet illustrates the idiom.
[SAMIN-DURR:79:18/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | هل لك is the predicate of an omitted subject, with إلى أن attached to that subject; the understood phrase is هل لك سبيل إلى التزكية.
